newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - NEW ZEALAND NEWSPAPERS - AUG 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - NEW ZEALAND NEWSPAPERS - AUG 7.

text.p: Injured Kiwi pulled girl from burning plane: A New Zealander who survived a jumbo jet crash in Guam on Wednesday is being credited with saving an 11-year-old girl. Page 1.

Feuding ministers summoned: Warring health ministers Bill English and Neil Kirton, whose relationship hit a new low on Wednesday when English suggested Kirton's behaviour left the government open to accusations of sleaze, appear before the coalition's leaders. Page 1.

Audit Office clears Kirton of awarding publicity job: An Audit Office has cleared Associate Health Minister Neil Kirton of awarding a health policy publicity contract to an advertising agency run by his brother-in-law. Page 2.

Mana Motuhake considered expelling Kopu -- Anderton: Mana Motuhake had considered expelling MP Alamein Kopu because she had not been attending Parliament as required, Alliance leader Jim Anderton said on Wednesday. Page 2.
East seeks approval for two new prisons: Corrections Minister Paul East will seek government approval to build two new prisons to cope with intense pressure on existing prisons' capacity. Page 2.

Iacocca ranks New Zealand top of economic class: American business icon Lee Iacocca said on Wednesday he was "awed" by the results of economic restructuring in New Zealand, but warned the country should not stand still. Page 13.
'Plot' by Govt on Kopu: The government has been accused of conniving in the decision of list MP Alamein Kopu to quit the Alliance. Page 5.

Lyttelton Port eyes Aust opportunities: Lyttelton Port Company is looking across the Tasman as one option to expand. The company on Wednesday announced a profit of $12.29 million in the year ended June 30, up 17.4 percent on the 1996 result. Page 24.
NZ Post out of bid: New Zealand Post is believed to have been forced out of the market for the Freightways courier business. Page 24.

Pac Retail signals new-format stores: Listed appliance and electrical goods retailer Pacific Retail Group is sticking with its forecast of a $6 million pre-tax profit for the six months to September, the annual meeting was told on Wednesday. Page 24.
Prime pays $4.1 for licences: An Australian broadcaster has paid about $4.15 million for a set of New Zealand-wide television frequencies. Page 24.
NZ Salmon likely to delist next year: New Zealand Salmon Company is unlikely to be delisted and wound up until next year. Page 24.

PM talks tough on Kirton impasse: The Prime Minister Jim Bolger flexed with his authority within the ruling coalition on Wednesday night, demanding that New Zealand First's junior minister, Neil Kirton, bow to the seniority of Bill English in the health portfolio -- or face the sack.

Nauru releases mortgage on Cooks hotel: Nauru has finally released a lien on the troubled Rarotongan Resort Hotel in the Cook Islands, clearing a major obstacle to its long-awaited sale. The government has already agreed to sell the hotel to an Auckland company.
